entries.note: Fukuzawa 2017 (PMID 28439081, PMC5430875) full text: quote verbatim. Opener untested before patient data is right; crovalimab is a member.

Bundle 761108 review: quote near-verbatim (column text inserts 'effectiveness'). Assay first public 2018, after eculizumab's PNH C5 blockade (2004): retro, retrodiction true. Ravulizumab, iv, unselected correct.
Quote verbatim in Fukuzawa full text; the monkey regimen was IV load then SC every two weeks at 2 mg/kg. Opener untested is right.

Bundle 761108: quote and NOD-scid '>3-fold longer half-life' verbatim. Sheridan 2018 PLoS One epub 12 Apr 2018, after ravulizumab's own PNH dose data (EHA/ASH 2016): retro under the dose rule. Ravulizumab, iv correct.

Röth 2020 abstract quote verbatim. Chugai release 6 Dec 2018: complete inhibition in all patients, IV load then weekly SC from day 36, so year 2018 holds; prospective (Fukuzawa 2017 predates own patient data). Crovalimab, sc correct.
Same Fukuzawa sentence; untested opener fine. No PNH animal model exists, so the human-serum lysis assay is the system relied on.

Bundle 761108 review quote verbatim (FDA's assessment). Study 301 NI co-primaries (transfusion avoidance, LDH normalisation) both met; design in note. Eculizumab's PNH efficacy predates the assay: retro. Ravulizumab, iv, unselected correct.
NCT02946463 eligibility criterion 5 verbatim; start 2016-12-12, so year 2016 is right.

Quote verbatim; review adds 'No meningococcal infection/sepsis was reported in the Phase 3 studies.' BB5.1 surrogate toxicology confirmed; not scoring the mouse's silence is right because it cannot show Neisseria susceptibility.

Abstract quote verbatim ('As expected...'). Could not see the full-text 'As predicted'/supplemental Fig 2 sentences. FDA 761388 has a Type III hypersensitivity section, so the harm is real. model_change true is misused because no contra precedes it; this is a separate harm.
Europe PMC full text PMC5430875 (Sci Rep, 24 Apr 2017) has the quote verbatim. Opening untested at 2017 with prediction_level patient is right; the assay predates COMPOSER's R885H dosing.

Chugai release 6 Dec 2018 verified: Part 2 'including two C5 SNP patients', 'Complete complement inhibition was achieved for all PNH patients treated'; year 2018 holds. Nishimura 2022 (PMID 35608260) has no abstract, Wiley 403: quote unseen. Crovalimab, sc, biomarker_selected right.
Bundle 761108 MultidisciplineR: quote verbatim. The EOP2 meeting on 18 Jul 2016 agreed the regimen, so year 2016 untested, class level.

The quote is verbatim in the bundle review next to the model's Ctrough >175 µg/mL target. The model was fitted to Phase 1/2 and set before Phase 3, so it is prospective: same, not retro. registry_date 2019-02-12 looks like a results date, not trial registration (2016).
Bundle 761388 IntegratedR: MIDD request quote verbatim (14 Mar 2019); EOP2 was 17 Jul 2019. Opening untested at 2019, class level, is right.

entries.rule: Evidence rule 6 (dating: earliest public date, label/regulator review)
entries.note: Cosson 2025 (epub 21 Jan 2025) quote verbatim; final PopPK fitted to Phase 3, retro right. But FDA BLA 761388 integrated review (June 2024, bundle) already gives the 92.8%/91.4% simulations and observed 94.8%/91.2% above 100 µg/mL: year 2024.
entries.adjudication_note: Both agree retro (rule 4: final PopPK fitted to COMMODORE data). Rule 6: FDA BLA 761388 integrated review (2024) already sets 92.8%/91.4% simulated against 94.8%/91.2% observed, so year should be 2024, not 2025.

entries.note: Röth 2020 abstract (PMID 31978221) quote verbatim. Chugai release 6 Dec 2018 verified ('Complete complement inhibition was achieved for all PNH patients treated'): year 2018. Post-eculizumab model: retro. Crovalimab, sc (IV load, SC maintenance), unselected correct.

Quote verbatim in bundle 761108 review (pharmacology). Opener of the ravulizumab track, untested before its patient comparison; year 2018 is a proxy (model_id first use 2017). Not the latest on track, so no untested_reason needed. Ravulizumab, iv correct.

Roche release 11 Dec 2022 quote as given; single-arm COMMODORE 3, co-primaries met, design in note. Higher-tier records (ASH 2022 abstract, Liu 2023) give the same status, still 2022. Post-eculizumab: retro. Crovalimab, sc, unselected correct.
Same verbatim 761108 pharmacology sentence as engagement 6. Opener of the ravulizumab efficacy track, untested before Study 301/302; year 2018 proxy. Ravulizumab, iv, unselected correct.

missing: Pozelimab + cemdisiran (ACCESS-1, NCT05133531; Regeneron press release and Lancet 2026) was positive against ravulizumab in PNH. The combination includes an siRNA, so it is optional in patient_trials and does not change status. Source: https://pmlive.com/pharma_news/regeneron-shares-positive-late-stage-results-for-poze-cemdi-in-rare-blood-disorder-pnh/

Tesidolumab: Novartis stopped development in favour of iptacopan, a strategic choice and not an efficacy failure. Worth a note so it is not read as a failure. Source: NCT02534909 / Novartis trial results.
Pozelimab's FDA review in the bundle (BLA 761339) is for CHAPLE disease, not PNH. It cannot serve as a PNH source, and the draft correctly does not use it.

COMMODORE 1 C5-polymorphism cohort (FDA crovalimab integrated review 2024, BLA 761388): one subject 'discontinued the study treatment on or after 24 weeks of treatment due to lack of efficacy'. It is a later patient result for the c5-r885h-variant-hemolysis-assay track and has no entry of its own. The cohort's genotype-level hemolysis data should be sought before it is scored.
corrections_fields_only: No status changes. Field fixes: model_change on dose 2, dose 3 and safety 3; NCT04434092 patient_trials doi/quote mismatch; dose 3 note's dosing frequency.
rule_questions: Dose: the monkey-based paper claimed a recycling antibody needs 'a much lower trough' than the ~99 µg/mL a conventional antibody needs, yet patients needed ~100 µg/mL. The regimen still worked. Is a wrong qualitative exposure claim with a working regimen 'same' with magnitude opposite or unquantified, or 'contra' (target too low)? Decision 16 and the dose table do not cover this case.

Efficacy for a follow-on member (ravulizumab) rested on non-inferiority to a non-member (eculizumab) plus an engagement assay. Does that count as an efficacy model, or as 'no disease model relied on' (empty list)? It is close to the cross-indication case but sits in the same indication.
model_change: is it meant only for turning a cell back after a contra, or also for any switch of model between entries? The draft uses it for both, and lint does not check it.

Safety cell with two distinct harms (meningococcal infection; DTDC hypersensitivity), each predicted by a different model: should these be separate entries scored independently, or one entry per change of best-model status as now?
